mainTopic: Whether מתנות כהונה can be claimed: defending רב חסדא's exemption, רב's doubt about a לוי, and the sources for the gifts to the poor
overview: This amud keeps testing רב חסדא's rule that someone who destroys or eats מתנות כהונה does not have to pay, because no single כהן can claim them. The גמרא first finishes an earlier answer: in that case a specific כהן already owned the טבל. Then it pushes away three more challenges. In the first, the king's men seize a threshing floor to pay a debt, and the owner must tithe only because he benefited. In the second, a משנה about buying a cow's innards deals with gifts that are still intact. In the third, a list of nine 'נכסי כהן' only means a כהן may use those items like his own money. Next comes a story about a לוי who snatched the gifts. רב's reaction is explained as coming from his doubt whether לוים count as 'עם'. רב אידי בר אבין challenges this from a ברייתא about gifts for the poor and the מתנות כהונה. Before explaining that challenge, the גמרא gives the פסוקים behind the vineyard gifts, and it starts on the grain gifts, which continue on the next amud.

steps.title: The gifts reached the כהן while still untithed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes defending רב חסדא. The earlier ברייתא, which made someone pay, is about produce that the כהן already owned while it was still טבל. This תנא holds that unseparated gifts are treated as already separated.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where the produce came into the כהן's hands while still untithed, and this תנא holds that gifts not yet separated are considered as if they were separated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering a challenge it raised earlier against רב חסדא. It explains that the earlier case is special, because the כהן already owned the produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא's rule covers gifts that no particular כהן owns yet, so nobody can sue for them. In this case one specific כהן already took possession of the produce while it was טבל. Since this תנא treats the gift portion as if it were already separated, that portion already belongs to him, and he can demand payment for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from which תרומה and מעשרות have not yet been separated
The gifts owed to the כהן (or the לוי)
Were separated (taken off from the produce)
Considered as though they were already separated
The author of a משנה or ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: This does not cancel רב חסדא's rule. It only explains why this particular case is different: here a specific כהן already owned the produce, so there is a real claimant.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that מתנות שלא הורמו כמי שהורמו דמיין is a famous dispute between תנאים. Here it is used to explain how a כהן can own a gift that has not yet been separated.

phrases.english: where they came into his hands while still untithed,
phrases.notes: "His hands" means the כהן's. He took the produce before anything was separated from it.

phrases.english: and this tanna holds:
gifts that have not been separated
are considered as though they have been separated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer to a challenge raised just before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) together with a view held by one תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The earlier ברייתא seemed to require payment for eaten gifts, which would go against רב חסדא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Payment is required only because a specific כהן already owned the טבל, and the gift portion counts as already separated.

steps.title: The king's men seize a threshing floor
steps.stepSummary: A new challenge to רב חסדא. If the king's men seized a man's grain to pay off his debt, he must still tithe. If they took it for no reason, he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if the king's household seized a man's threshing floor, then if it was for his debt, he must tithe; if it was taken by force for no reason, he is exempt from tithing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to go against רב חסדא. The owner must tithe grain he no longer even has, as if the gifts were money he owes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The grain was taken to pay a debt, yet the owner must still give מעשר for it. That makes it look as though the tithe is a real money obligation with a claimant. If so, a כהן or לוי could collect it, which goes against רב חסדא's idea of ממון שאין לו תובעים.

keyTerms.meaning: Threshing floor (here, the grain on it)
Seized by force
As payment of his debt
Taken by force, for no reason or claim
To separate מעשר (tithe)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
where the king's household seized his threshing floor by force,
if it was for his debt, he is obligated to tithe,
if it was for no reason, he is exempt from tithing.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הֲרֵי שֶׁאָנְסוּ בֵּית הַמֶּלֶךְ גׇּרְנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the last challenge was answered, a new source is brought against רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that the gifts are ממון שאין לו תובעים, so no payment is required
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Requiring tithes for grain seized to pay a debt makes the tithe look like a real money obligation that someone could claim.

steps.title: He benefited from the seizure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes the proof away. In the debt case the man must tithe because the seized grain paid off his debt, so he gained from it. It is not because a כהן could sue him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because he gains benefit from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge. It shows that the ברייתא has a different reason for requiring the tithe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain taken for his debt cancelled what he owed, so it is as if he used untithed grain to pay a debt. Since he benefited from it, he must tithe. This has nothing to do with whether the gifts have a claimant, so רב חסדא's rule still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there
He benefits from it (literally, it takes root for him)

phrases.english: It is different there,
since he gains benefit from it.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the attempt to use the threshing-floor ברייתא against רב חסדא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The duty to tithe comes from the benefit he got, not from the gifts having a claimant.

steps.title: Buying a cow's innards that include the gifts
steps.stepSummary: Another challenge begins, quoting a משנה. If someone bought a cow's innards and the מתנות כהונה were among them, the buyer gives them to the כהן. Whether he gets money back depends on whether he bought by weight.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if one said to a butcher, 'Sell me the innards of a cow,' and the priestly gifts were among them, he gives them to the כהן and does not deduct their value from the price. If he bought by weight, he gives them to the כהן and deducts their value from the price.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a משנה to set up another challenge to רב חסדא. The actual argument from this משנה comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When he simply bought 'the innards,' the gifts were never part of the sale, so he pays nothing extra and gets nothing back. When he bought by weight, he paid for the gifts too, so the butcher must return their value. The משנה treats the gifts as something that must reach the כהן and as worth money, and the גמרא will use that to test רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: The innards (they include the קיבה, one of the priestly gifts)
The priestly gifts from an animal: זרוע, לחיים, and קיבה
Deducts (lowers the price)
The money, the price
By weight

phrases.english: Come and hear: if one said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is the butcher who is selling the meat.

phrases.aramaic: מְכוֹר לִי בְּנֵי מֵעֶיהָ שֶׁל פָּרָה,
phrases.english: Sell me the innards of the cow,
and the gifts of the priesthood were among them,
he gives them to the priest,
and he does not deduct for him from the money.
If he bought from him by weight,
he gives them to the priest,
and he deducts for him from the money.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, אָמַר לוֹ: מְכוֹר לִי בְּנֵי מֵעֶיהָ שֶׁל פָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the threshing-floor challenge was rejected, a new source is brought.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's rule that the priestly gifts are ממון שאין לו תובעים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה treats the gifts as having real value that must go to the כהן. The exact inference is spelled out in Step 5.

steps.title: Why should the buyer have to give the gifts at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the challenge from the משנה. Selling the innards should count like damaging or eating the gifts, and רב חסדא says that person is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why must the buyer give the gifts to the כהן? Selling them should be just like damaging or eating the מתנות כהונה, and for that a person is exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now spells out the attack that the משנה from Step 4 was setting up. If the butcher sold the gifts, he got rid of them, and that looks just like damaging or eating them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא ruled that someone who damages or eats מתנות כהונה does not have to pay, because no single כהן can sue for them. The משנה, however, makes the gifts go to the כהן even after they were sold to someone else. That seems to show the gifts can be claimed, which goes against רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: Why? It opens a challenge.
One who damages
The gifts given to a כהן from a slaughtered animal: the foreleg, the jaw and the maw

phrases.english: Why?
phrases.notes: He means: why must the buyer hand over the gifts in the case from the משנה?

phrases.english: Let it be like one who damages the gifts of the priesthood
or who ate them!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? לֶיהֱוֵי כְּמַזִּיק מַתְּנוֹת כְּהוּנָּה אוֹ שֶׁאֲכָלָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge whose source was quoted in Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that one who damages or eats מתנות כהונה is exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה makes the gifts go to the כהן even after they were sold. That suggests the gifts can be claimed by a כהן, which contradicts the exemption.

steps.title: The gifts are still physically there
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה's case is different, because the gifts are still intact.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because the gifts are still there in their original form.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the challenge away. In the משנה, the gifts have not been destroyed. They are sitting right there in the buyer's hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא only exempts someone when the gifts are gone, because they were damaged or eaten. When the actual gifts still exist, whoever is holding them must simply hand them over. So the משנה does not contradict רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there. Used to set a source apart from the case being discussed.
They are intact, still in their original form

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as saying a כהן can sue for the gifts. The point is only that intact gifts must be handed over. Once they are destroyed, there is no payment.

phrases.english: It is different there,
since they are intact.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the משנה about the innards
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה deals with gifts that still exist. רב חסדא deals with gifts that were destroyed.

steps.title: A list of nine items called the property of a כהן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new source: nine items, including the gifts, are called 'property of a כהן'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: nine items are the property of a כהן: תרומה, תרומת מעשר, חלה, the first shearing, the gifts, דמאי, ביכורים, the principal and the fifth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that lists nine things belonging to a כהן. This sets up a new challenge to רב חסדא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list includes 'מתנות', the very gifts רב חסדא was talking about. If they are truly called the כהן's property, that could suggest he can claim them like any other money he is owed.

keyTerms.meaning: Property of a כהן
The first wool shorn from sheep, given to a כהן
Produce bought from someone not trusted to have tithed it
The principal and the added fifth paid for stolen property

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Nine items are the property of a priest:
teruma, teruma of the tithe, and ḥalla,
the first shearing, the gifts, and demai,
phrases.notes: For דמאי, the כהן gets the תרומת מעשר that is separated from it.

phrases.english: the first fruits, the principal, and the fifth.
phrases.notes: The principal and the fifth are the repayment for something stolen from a convert who died with no heirs. It goes to the כהן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a fresh challenge to רב חסדא after the previous one was answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that the gifts cannot be claimed in court
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source is quoted here. The actual inference comes in the next step.

steps.title: Does 'property' mean the כהן can take them through judges?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the inference: calling them property must mean they can be taken through בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what purpose are they called his property? Is it not so that he can take them out through judges?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses the list to attack רב חסדא. It suggests that 'property of a כהן' means a כהן can go to court to get these items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a כהן can force the owner through judges to hand over the gifts, then the gifts do have someone who can claim them. That would make the person who destroyed them liable to pay, against רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: To take them out by means of judges, meaning to collect them through a court
For what purpose?

phrases.english: For what purpose?
Is it not to extract them through judges?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the list quoted in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's exemption for one who damages or eats the gifts
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Property' suggests the items can be claimed in court. Items that can be claimed should make the person who destroyed them liable.

steps.title: 'Property' means he may use them like his own money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'property of a כהן' only means that once he has them, he may use them for anything, as a משנה explains.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is as we learned: why did they call these the property of a כהן? Because he may buy with them slaves, land and a non-kosher animal. A creditor may take them for his debt, a wife may take them for her כתובה, and he may buy a ספר תורה with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the inference. It quotes a משנה showing that 'property of a כהן' is about how he may use the items after he receives them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike קדשים, these items are fully the כהן's own money once they reach him. He can trade them, pay debts with them, and so on. This says nothing about forcing anyone in court to hand them over, so רב חסדא still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A creditor
The marriage contract payment owed to a wife
A non-kosher animal

steps.whatToRemember: 'נכסי כהן' means the gifts are fully the כהן's own money once he holds them. It does not mean he can sue to get them. רב חסדא's ruling survives this challenge too.

phrases.english: No, it is for that which we learned:
Why did they say 'property of a priest'?
Because he may buy slaves and lands with them
and a non-kosher animal,
and a creditor takes them for his debt,
and a wife takes them for her marriage contract,
and he may buy a Torah scroll with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לִכְדִתְנַן: לָמָה אָמְרוּ נִכְסֵי כֹהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the inference drawn in Step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the list of nine 'נכסי כהן'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'property' refers to what the כהן may do with the items once he has them, not to collecting them in court.

steps.title: A לוי who snatched the gifts
steps.stepSummary: A לוי kept snatching מתנות כהונה. רב reacted: it is enough that we do not take the gifts from him, and now he also snatches them?
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain לוי who used to snatch the gifts. People came and told רב. He said to them: Is it not enough for him that we do not take the gifts from him? Must he also snatch them?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. רב is upset with a לוי who grabbed מתנות כהונה that were meant for a כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב points out that this לוי already gets a break, since the gifts are not taken from his own animals. Using that as a reason to grab gifts that belong to כהנים is going too far.

keyTerms.meaning: A לוי
Snatches, grabs
Is it not enough for him?

phrases.english: There was a certain Levite who would snatch the gifts,
they came and told Rav,
he said to them:
Is it not enough for him that we do not take from him,
phrases.notes: He means: from his own animals, we do not take the מתנות כהונה.

phrases.english: but he also snatches?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section, a story about a לוי and the gifts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A לוי is not made to give the gifts from his own animals, but he certainly may not snatch gifts that belong to כהנים.

steps.title: What Does רב Really Hold About a לוי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב's position. Either a לוי is part of 'the people' and must give, or he is not and is fully exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does רב hold? If לוים are called 'people,' we should also take the gifts from them. If they are not called 'people,' the Torah exempted them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב's half-way position from the last step: we don't take the gifts from a לוי, but he also shouldn't snatch them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק obligates 'the people' to give the gifts. If a לוי is included, we should force him to give. If he is not included, he owes nothing, and רב should have no complaint against him. A middle position seems to make no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The people,' the word in the פסוק that defines who must give the gifts
'The Merciful One,' a way of referring to God or the Torah
Exempted them

phrases.english: And Rav: if they are called 'people'
phrases.notes: This points to the פסוק 'מאת העם' (דברים 18:3), which says who has to give these gifts.

phrases.english: then let one also take the gifts from them.
If they are not called 'people'
the Merciful One exempted them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the logic of רב's reaction in Step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's position that we don't take from a לוי, yet he may not snatch
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A dilemma. Either the לוי is obligated, so we should take from him, or he is exempt, so he has done nothing wrong.

steps.title: רב Was Unsure
steps.stepSummary: רב was unsure whether לוים count as 'the people,' which explains his middle position.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is unsure whether they are called 'people' or not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רב was in doubt about whether a לוי counts as 'the people.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because it is a doubt, we cannot force the לוי to give, since we are not sure he owes anything. But because he might owe the gifts, he has no right to snatch them for himself either. A doubt explains both halves of רב's statement.

keyTerms.meaning: He is in doubt; he is unsure
A doubt, an unresolved question

steps.whatToRemember: רב's position comes from a doubt. We can't take the gifts from a לוי, but he may not grab them either.

phrases.english: He is unsure
whether they are called 'people'
or whether they are not called 'people'.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a third option: a doubt
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב had to hold either that לוים are definitely obligated or definitely exempt
steps.terutzMaskana: רב was in doubt, so the gifts can't be taken from a לוי and he can't snatch them

steps.title: רב אידי בר אבין Quotes the List of Gifts for the Poor
steps.stepSummary: While רב פפא was teaching רב's ruling, רב אידי בר אבין began a challenge from a ברייתא that lists the gifts left for the poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא was sitting and teaching this ruling. רב אידי בר אבין objected from a ברייתא: There are four gifts for the poor in a vineyard: single fallen grapes, underdeveloped clusters, forgotten clusters, and the corner. There are three in grain: gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner. There are two in a tree: forgotten fruit and the corner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. Here we only get the list of gifts for the poor. The key line that makes the challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This first part of the ברייתא just names the gifts the poor receive from vineyards, grain fields, and trees. It prepares the ground for the ברייתא's ruling about who may keep these gifts, which is aimed at רב's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or ruling
Gifts the Torah gives to the poor from the harvest
Single grapes that fall during picking
Small, underdeveloped grape clusters
Produce forgotten in the field
The corner of the field left for the poor

phrases.english: Rav Pappa was sitting and saying
this teaching,
phrases.notes: He means רב's ruling about the לוי from the last steps.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Idi bar Avin raised an objection to Rav Pappa:
Four gifts for the poor in a vineyard:
the single fallen grapes, and the underdeveloped clusters,
and the forgotten clusters, and the corner;
and three in grain:
the gleanings, and the forgotten sheaves, and the corner;
two in a tree:
the forgotten fruit and the corner.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין לְרַב פָּפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against רב's ruling as explained in Step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that we do not take the gifts from a לוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only. The ברייתא's list of gifts for the poor is quoted before its key ruling.

steps.title: Even a Poor Owner Must Give Up the Poor Gifts
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that the owner gets no say over who receives these gifts. Even a poor owner has them taken from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: None of these gifts give the owner the benefit of choosing who receives them. Even if the owner is a poor Jew, the court takes them from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא that רב אידי בר אבין is quoting continues. A poor owner cannot keep the poor gifts for himself; בית דין takes them from him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A poor owner is exactly the kind of person who receives these gifts, yet he still cannot keep his own, and בית דין takes them from him. This is still part of the ברייתא that רב אידי בר אבין is quoting. The line about the לוי, which the challenge rests on, comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The benefit of choosing which person receives your gift
The owner of the field or produce
A poor person
They take it out of his hand, meaning the court takes it from him

steps.confusionAlert: The poor owner here is not stealing from others. He simply has to leave his field's gifts for other poor people, even though he is poor himself.

phrases.english: All of them do not have
the benefit of choice for the owner,
phrases.notes: The owner can't pick which poor person gets them. Any poor person may come and take.

phrases.english: and even a poor Jew who owns the field
they take it from his hand.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלָּן אֵין בָּהֶם טוֹבַת הֲנָאָה לַבְּעָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא begun in Step 13; the ברייתא finishes in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that we do not take the gifts from a לוי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This step continues the ברייתא. The objection rests on the ברייתא's later line about the לוי (Step 15), and the גמרא explains it after this amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא finishes: מעשר עני versus the other מתנות כהונה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by contrasting מעשר עני, where the owner chooses the recipient, with the other מתנות כהונה, which are never taken away from a כהן or a לוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: מעשר עני, which is handed out from inside the owner's house, is different: the owner gets to choose who receives it. Even a poor Jew must separate it, and the court takes it from him. But the other מתנות כהונה, like the foreleg, the jaws and the maw, are not taken away from the owner. They are not taken from one כהן to give to another כהן, and not from one לוי to give to another לוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא that רב אידי בר אבין started in order to challenge רב. The last line is the key part: the מתנות כהונה are not taken from a לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gifts left in the field belong to whichever poor person comes, but מעשר עני is given out at home, so the owner picks the recipient. The last line says בית דין does not take the זרוע, לחיים and קבה away, not from one כהן to another and not from one לוי to another. This mention of a לוי is what רב אידי בר אבין will use against רב, and the גמרא explains his objection after it finishes giving sources for the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The tithe for the poor, separated in certain years of the cycle
The owner's right to choose who receives his gift
The court takes it out of his hands by force
The foreleg, the jaws and the maw, the gifts given to a כהן from a slaughtered animal

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse the two halves. The first half (מעשר עני) is taken from the owner by בית דין. The second half (זרוע, לחיים, קבה) is not taken from him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This line about the לוי is the base of רב אידי בר אבין's challenge to רב, who said the gifts are not taken from a לוי but that a לוי still may not snatch them.

phrases.english: The poor man's tithe, which is distributed inside his house –
the owner has the right to choose who gets it,
and even a poor person in Israel,
phrases.notes: Even though he is poor himself, he still has to separate this tithe from his own produce.

phrases.english: they take it out of his hands,
and the other gifts of the כהונה,
such as the foreleg, the jaws and the maw –
they do not take them out of his hands,
not from a כהן to give to another כהן
and not from a לוי to give to another לוי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the ברייתא begun in steps 13-14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling about the לוי, which rests on his doubt whether לוים are called 'עם'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא mentions that the gifts are not taken 'from a לוי to a לוי.' רב אידי בר אבין's objection to רב is based on this line. The גמרא spells out the objection after its detour into sources.

steps.title: The four vineyard gifts and the verse for two of them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pauses to give the source for the ברייתא's list of four vineyard gifts, starting with פרט and עוללות.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are four gifts from a vineyard: פרט, עוללות, שכחה and פאה. As it is written: 'And you shall not glean your vineyard, and you shall not gather the fallen grapes of your vineyard.'
steps.whatsHappening: Before explaining רב אידי בר אבין's challenge, the גמרא stops to show where the ברייתא's vineyard gifts come from. This פסוק covers פרט and עוללות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's list included four vineyard gifts. 'לא תעולל' is the source for עוללות, and 'ופרט כרמך לא תלקט' is the source for פרט. The next steps give sources for שכחה and פאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Single grapes that fall off during the harvest
Small, poorly formed grape clusters
Clusters the harvester forgot
A corner of the field or vineyard left for the poor

phrases.english: Four gifts of the vineyard:
the fallen grapes, and the small clusters,
and the forgotten clusters, and the corner,
as it is written: 'And your vineyard you shall not glean,
and the fallen grapes of your vineyard you shall not gather.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side detour giving the source for the vineyard gifts listed in the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The ברייתא's list of four vineyard gifts
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 19:10, the source for עוללות and פרט

steps.title: The word 'after you' teaches forgotten clusters
steps.stepSummary: A second פסוק about the vineyard says 'after you,' and רבי לוי says this word teaches שכחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is written: 'When you harvest your vineyard, you shall not glean after you.' רבי לוי said: 'After you' refers to שכחה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another פסוק about the vineyard to find the source for שכחה in a vineyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'אחריך' points to clusters the harvester already passed and left behind him. Those are forgotten clusters, so this is the source for שכחה in a vineyard.

keyTerms.meaning: You harvest grapes
After you, behind you

phrases.english: And it is written: 'When you harvest your vineyard,
you shall not glean after you,'
רבי לוי said:
'After you' – this is the forgotten clusters.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְתִיב: ״כִּי תִבְצֹר כַּרְמְךָ לֹא תְעוֹלֵל אַחֲרֶיךָ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the source search, now for שכחה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 24:21, as explained by רבי לוי

steps.title: Corner of the vineyard learned from the olive tree
steps.stepSummary: פאה in a vineyard is learned from the matching word 'after you' in the פסוק about olive trees, where the תורה says to leave some of the tree's 'splendor' for the poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: פאה is learned by matching 'after you' here with 'after you' about the olive tree, as it is written: 'When you beat your olive tree, you shall not go over the branches after you.' And the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: This means you should not take all of its splendor from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the source search by finding פאה for a vineyard. It uses the same word 'after you' that appears in the פסוק about olives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a גזירה שוה: the word 'אחריך' appears both by the vineyard and by the olive tree. By olives, 'לא תפאר' means do not strip the tree of all its glory, so you must leave a part for the poor. The matching word teaches that a vineyard also needs a portion left as פאה.

keyTerms.meaning: He learns it, here by matching the same word in two פסוקים
You beat, knocking olives off the tree
Do not take all of the tree's splendor, meaning leave some for the poor
Its splendor, its glory

steps.whatToRemember: All four vineyard gifts in the ברייתא have sources: פרט and עוללות from ויקרא, שכחה from 'אחריך,' and פאה from matching 'אחריך' with the olive tree. After this detour, the גמרא will go back to רב אידי בר אבין's challenge.

phrases.english: The corner – it is learned from 'after you,' 'after you,' from the olive tree,
phrases.notes: The same word appears in both פסוקים, so a rule from the olive tree carries over to the vineyard.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'When you beat your olive tree,
you shall not go over the branches after you,'
and the school of רבי ישמעאל taught:
that you should not take its splendor from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the sources for the four vineyard gifts by giving the source for פאה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A matching-word link from דברים 24:20 about olives, with the explanation of the school of רבי ישמעאל

steps.title: Turning to the three grain gifts, starting with gleanings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the ברייתא: three gifts come from grain, and the first is לקט. This begins the search for their sources.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא said: there are three gifts from grain. The first is the gleanings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It quotes the ברייתא's line about the three grain gifts, starting with לקט, so it can show where each one comes from in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 16 to 18 gave sources for the four vineyard gifts. Now the גמרא moves to a new group in the same list, the gifts from a grain field. Quoting the words of the ברייתא here is the opening for the source that will come next.

keyTerms.meaning: Grain, the crop of a field such as wheat or barley
Gleanings: one or two stalks that fall during harvest and must be left for the poor
Gifts the farmer must leave for the poor

phrases.english: Three that are from grain:
the gleanings,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the sources for the vineyard gifts, the גמרא moves on to the grain gifts from the same ברייתא list.
steps.raayaObject: The ברייתא's statement that לקט is one of the three gifts left to the poor from grain
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's own list. The פסוק that serves as the source is expected to come in the next line.
